failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: The answers followed salient associations or overly narrow candidates instead of the requested target and all distinguishing clue details.

rejected_edits.content: When the requested taxonomic group has a conventional plural name, use that canonical plural form even if the clue refers to it with a singular demonstrative such as “this.” Do not mechanically singularize the category name; otherwise, match the grammatical number requested by the clue.
rejected_edits.target: For direct definition or trivia clues, treat the description as a fill-in target and return the conventional term or category called for by the whole clue, including after elliptical wording such as “one of these.” Match the requested grammatical number; when the answer is a singular count noun, include its conventional indefinite article. Do not answer with a named example when the clue asks for its class, or repeat an embedded synonym that serves only as a cue rather than the target.

rejected_edits.content: When a clue is framed as “In this book [character or event detail],” treat the detail as identifying evidence and return the book’s title. Do not fact-check or correct the embedded claim unless the prompt explicitly asks whether it is true.
rejected_edits.target: For a prompt consisting only of a named work, slogan, or quoted expression, with or without a year, infer the intended identifying relation from context rather than defaulting to a definition or classification. When context clearly links the expression to a person or entity being identified, give that attribution; if the prompt asks for the expression's type or meaning, answer that instead. For a quoted catchphrase that also appears in a related work's title, prefer the familiar source work or speaker when context treats the phrase as a catchphrase; return the matching title only when the prompt or context clearly asks for that work.
